where: Section 1, last sentence ("Its weakness is wiring: each direction and each parameter needs its own pair")
problem: A 32-bit ARINC 429 word carries a label, and one transmitter pair sends many different labels one after another (time-multiplexed). The standard requires one pair per direction (one transmitter per pair, up to 20 receivers); it does not require one pair per parameter. Saying a pair is needed for every parameter teaches a false rule and also drives the answer to Q4.
fix: Write: each direction needs its own pair, because a 429 pair has only one transmitter. One pair can carry many parameters as a stream of labelled words; a dedicated transmitter is a design choice made when a parameter needs a high, independent update rate.

problem: The question says "20 one-way parameters to send between two LRUs", which does not say whether the 20 parameters travel one way or both ways, and the model answer (20 pairs + 20 pairs) assumes one pair per parameter, a design choice rather than a standard requirement.
fix: State the direction, e.g. "20 parameters must go from LRU A to LRU B, and 20 back". Answer: 429 needs one pair per direction per transmitter, so 20 pairs each way if each parameter gets its own transmitter, fewer if labels are multiplexed on shared pairs; 1553B needs one shared bus (two cables if dual redundant) plus a bus controller, with command/status overhead and a 1 Mbps limit shared by all 40 transfers.

where: Worked example 1 and Quiz Q7 (word counting)
problem: The counts (1 command + 1 data + 1 status, and 1 command + 4 data + 1 status) match only a transmit message (RT to controller). In the receive message described in Q6 and in the figure, the RT sends a status word after the command and again after the data, so the same data needs one extra word. A student who follows Q6 and then answers Q7 gets a different total.
fix: Name the message type in both places. Transmit: command + status + n data words. Receive: command + status + n data words + final status. For 4 data words: 6 words = 120 µs transmit, 7 words = 140 µs receive, gaps ignored.
